tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 1
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A cooperative bank compounds its quoted $7.2\%$ nominal rate quarterly. The treasurer reports an annual effective yield of 7.40\%.
A museum places $24{,}000$ in a reserve growing continuously at $3.8\%$. Five years later, the curator values it at \$29{,}196.99.
A documentary contract pays royalties of $8{,}000$ after year 1, $11{,}000$ after year 3, and $15{,}000$ after year 5. At $6.2\%$ effective interest, the rights are worth \$27{,}820.41 today.
A songwriter receives $6{,}000$ in the first year, and each of the next five annual royalties is $7\%$ larger. The six checks total \$43{,}179.74.
A design studio leases software for 36 month-end payments of $420$ at a monthly rate of $0.55\%$. The lease liability at signing is \$13{,}683.22.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

An effective annual rate must reproduce the accumulation from every compounding period in the year.

$$i_p=\frac{0.0720}{4}=0.018000$$

$$1+R=(1+i_p)^{4}=(1+0.018000)^{4}$$

$$R=(1+0.018000)^{4}-1=0.07396743$$

$$100R=7.3967\%$$

The computed effective annual rate is 7.40\%, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Continuous growth applies the exponential accumulation factor to the opening principal.

$$FV=Pe^{rt}$$

$$FV=24000.00e^{(0.0380)(5)}$$

$$FV=24000.00e^{0.190000}$$

$$FV=29021.990344$$

The computed future value is \$29{,}021.99, not \$29{,}196.99, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

A constant percentage change makes the scheduled amounts a finite geometric progression.

$$C_k=6000.00(1.07000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_6=\sum_{k=1}^{6}6000.00(1.07000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_6=6000.00\frac{1.07000^{6}-1}{1.07000-1}$$

$$S_6=42919.744444$$

The computed schedule total is \$42{,}919.74, not \$43{,}179.74, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Value the level payments at the correct timing point, then adjust for advance or deferral when required.

$$a_{\overline{36}|}=\frac{1-(1+0.00550)^{-36}}{0.00550}$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}=420.00a_{\overline{36}|}=13683.215576$$

$$PV=13683.215576$$

The computed annuity present value is \$13{,}683.22, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 2
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A cleanup obligation of $85{,}000$ is payable seven years from now. Using a $4.1\%$ force of interest, the environmental auditor records \$63{,}553.50 today.
An insurer will reimburse a clinic $18{,}000$ in two years and $27{,}000$ in four years. A $5.5\%$ valuation rate gives a present claim value of \$37{,}967.00.
A renovation reserve releases $20{,}000$ in year 1, then cuts each later release by $12\%$ for four more years. The five releases add to \$78{,}371.35.
A swimmer saves $275$ after each month for 48 months in an account earning $0.45\%$ monthly. Immediately after the final deposit, the fund is \$14{,}697.29.
A chef finances a $310{,}000$ restaurant unit over 300 months at $0.47\%$ per month. The required month-end payment is \$1{,}953.68.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Discounting a continuously compounded liability reverses growth with a negative exponent.

$$PV=Fe^{-rt}$$

$$PV=85000.00e^{-(0.0410)(7)}$$

$$PV=85000.00e^{-0.287000}$$

$$PV=63793.496951$$

The computed present value is \$63{,}793.50, not \$63{,}553.50, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

Each dated cash flow requires its own discount exponent before the values can be added.

$$PV=\sum_{t}\frac{C_t}{(1+i)^t}$$

$$PV=\frac{18000.00}{(1+0.0550)^2}+\frac{27000.00}{(1+0.0550)^4}$$

$$PV_2=\frac{18000.00}{(1+0.0550)^2}=16172.143483$$

$$PV_4=\frac{27000.00}{(1+0.0550)^4}=21794.852069$$

$$PV=16172.143483+21794.852069$$

$$PV=37966.995552$$

The computed present value is \$37{,}967.00, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

A constant percentage change makes the scheduled amounts a finite geometric progression.

$$C_k=20000.00(0.88000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_5=\sum_{k=1}^{5}20000.00(0.88000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_5=20000.00\frac{0.88000^{5}-1}{0.88000-1}$$

$$S_5=78711.347200$$

The computed schedule total is \$78{,}711.35, not \$78{,}371.35, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

An ordinary annuity accumulates every end-of-period payment to the date of the last payment.

$$s_{\overline{48}|}=\frac{(1+0.00450)^48-1}{0.00450}$$

$$FV=275.00s_{\overline{48}|}$$

$$FV=275.00\frac{(1+0.00450)^48-1}{0.00450}$$

$$FV=14697.292644$$

The computed annuity future value is \$14{,}697.29, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=310000.00\frac{0.004700}{1-(1+0.004700)^{-300}}$$

$$PMT=1929.676239$$

The computed monthly payment is \$1{,}929.68, not \$1{,}953.68, so the statement is False.

tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A manufacturer offers rebates of $4{,}500$, $6{,}000$, and $7{,}500$ at the ends of the next three years. Discounting at $7.1\%$ produces \$15{,}537.63.

A gallery prepays through 10 annual rent installments of $8{,}000$, the first due immediately. At $5.2\%$, their present value is \$64{,}359.54.
After payment 60 on a $420{,}000$, 360-month clinic loan charging $0.42\%$ monthly, the remaining principal is \$385{,}048.96.
A cold-storage upgrade costs $180{,}000$ and returns $55{,}000$, $70{,}000$, and $95{,}000$ after years 1, 2, and 4. At $8.0\%$, its NPV is \$767.48.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → False

A constant percentage change makes the scheduled amounts a finite geometric progression.

$$C_k=4500.00(1.06667)^{k-1}$$

$$S_7=\sum_{k=1}^{7}4500.00(1.06667)^{k-1}$$

$$S_7=4500.00\frac{1.06667^{7}-1}{1.06667-1}$$

$$S_7=38548.575210$$

The computed schedule total is \$38{,}548.58, not \$38{,}763.58, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Value the level payments at the correct timing point, then adjust for advance or deferral when required.

$$a_{\overline{10}|}=\frac{1-(1+0.05200)^{-10}}{0.05200}$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}=8000.00a_{\overline{10}|}=61178.270096$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=(1+0.05200)PV_{\mathrm{ordinary}}$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=64359.540142$$

The computed annuity present value is \$64{,}359.54, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=420000.00\frac{0.004200}{1-(1+0.004200)^{-360}}$$

$$PMT=2264.929420$$

$$n_{\mathrm{remaining}}=360-60=300$$

$$B_60=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-300}}{i}$$

$$B_60=385898.961320$$

The computed balance after payment 60 is \$385{,}898.96, not \$385{,}048.96, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 4
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A machine shop deposits $3{,}000$ at the end of year 1 and increases each of the next five deposits by $5\%$. The account earns $6.5\%$. Immediately after deposit 6, it holds \$23{,}624.33.
A professorship pays $24{,}000$ at every year-end forever. With a $4.8\%$ spending rate, the required endowment is \$500{,}000.00.
A warehouse mortgage starts at $275{,}000$, runs 240 months, and charges $0.51\%$ monthly. The first payment reduces principal by \$604.77.
A timber parcel costs \$75{,}000 today and is expected to sell for \$118{,}000 in five years with no interim cash flows. Its IRR is 9.49\%.
A wholesaler finances inventory at $9.6\%$ nominal with monthly conversion. Its audit worksheet lists 9.82\% as the effective yearly borrowing rate.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

At the final deposit date, each growing contribution has earned a different number of interest periods.

$$FV=\sum_{k=0}^{5}3000.00(1+0.0500)^k(1+0.0650)^{5-k}$$

$$FV=3000.00(1+0.0650)^{5}\sum_{k=0}^{5}\left(\frac{1+0.0500}{1+0.0650}\right)^k$$

$$FV=3000.00(1+0.0650)^{5}\frac{1-0.98591549^6}{1-0.98591549}$$

$$FV=23809.331183$$

The computed accumulated balance is \$23{,}809.33, not \$23{,}624.33, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

The infinite payment stream converges because its discount rate exceeds its growth rate.

$$PV_1=\sum_{t=1}^\infty\frac{24000.00(1+0.0000)^{t-1}}{(1+0.0480)^t}$$

$$PV_1=\frac{24000.00}{0.0480-0.0000}$$

$$PV_1=500000.000000$$

The computed perpetuity present value is \$500{,}000.00, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=275000.00\frac{0.005100}{1-(1+0.005100)^{-240}}$$

$$PMT=1989.270603$$

$$I_1=275000.00(0.005100)=1402.500000$$

$$PR_1=PMT-I_1=1989.270603-1402.500000$$

$$PR_1=586.770603$$

The computed first principal reduction is \$586.77, not \$604.77, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

For one terminal inflow, the IRR is the compound rate that makes discounted inflow equal initial cost.

$$0=-75000.00+\frac{118000.00}{(1+r)^5}$$

$$75000.00(1+r)^5=118000.00$$

$$1+r=\left(\frac{118000.00}{75000.00}\right)^{1/5}$$

$$r=0.09487402$$

$$100r=9.4874\%$$

The computed internal rate of return is 9.49\%, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

An effective annual rate must reproduce the accumulation from every compounding period in the year.

$$i_p=\frac{0.0960}{12}=0.008000$$

$$1+R=(1+i_p)^{12}=(1+0.008000)^{12}$$

$$R=(1+0.008000)^{12}-1=0.10033869$$

$$100R=10.0339\%$$

The computed effective annual rate is 10.03\%, not 9.82\%, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 5
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A park receives $30{,}000$ next year and donations then grow $2\%$ annually forever. At a $6.5\%$ discount rate, the gift stream is worth \$666{,}666.67.
A $190{,}000$ studio loan is amortized with 180 monthly payments at $0.44\%$. Across the full schedule, interest totals \$84{,}515.95.
A language app requires \$96{,}000 now and produces $28{,}000$ annually for four years. Discounting at $9.5\%$ gives NPV -\$6{,}274.53.
A pension account promises a $6.8\%$ effective annual return. The monthly rate that reproduces that promise is 0.575\%.
A family trust earns continuously at $4.6\%$. Its algebraic doubling time is $15.07$ years.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The infinite payment stream converges because its discount rate exceeds its growth rate.

$$PV_1=\sum_{t=1}^\infty\frac{30000.00(1+0.0200)^{t-1}}{(1+0.0650)^t}$$

$$PV_1=\frac{30000.00}{0.0650-0.0200}$$

$$PV_1=666666.666667$$

The computed perpetuity present value is \$666{,}666.67, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=190000.00\frac{0.004400}{1-(1+0.004400)^{-180}}$$

$$PMT=1530.366392$$

$$\mathrm{Total\ payments}=180(1530.366392)=275465.950520$$

$$\mathrm{Interest}=275465.950520-190000.00$$

$$\mathrm{Interest}=85465.950520$$

The computed total interest is \$85{,}465.95, not \$84{,}515.95, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Equivalent periodic and annual rates have the same one-year accumulation factor.

$$(1+i_p)^{12}=1+0.0680$$

$$i_p=(1+0.0680)^{1/12}-1$$

$$i_p=0.00549737$$

$$100i_p=0.5497\%$$

The computed periodic rate is 0.550\%, not 0.575\%, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

The time is unknown, so take natural logarithms in the continuous accumulation equation.

$$2.0000=e^{0.0460t}$$

$$\ln(2.0000)=0.0460t$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(2.0000)}{0.0460}$$

$$t=15.068417$$

The computed elapsed time is $15.07$ years, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=520000.00\frac{0.003900}{1-(1+0.003900)^{-360}}$$

$$PMT=2690.669196$$

The computed monthly payment is \$2{,}690.67, not \$2{,}659.67, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

An effective annual rate must reproduce the accumulation from every compounding period in the year.

$$i_p=\frac{0.0560}{4}=0.014000$$

$$1+R=(1+i_p)^{4}=(1+0.014000)^{4}$$

$$R=(1+0.014000)^{4}-1=0.05718701$$

$$100R=5.7187\%$$

The computed effective annual rate is 5.72\%, not 5.84\%, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

A force of interest and an effective annual rate are equivalent when their one-year growth factors agree.

$$1+R=e^{0.0520}$$

$$R=e^{0.0520}-1$$

$$R=0.05337574$$

$$100R=5.3376\%$$

The computed effective annual rate is 5.34\%, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 7
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A rare manuscript bought for \$42{,}000 is sold six years later for $71{,}500$. With no other cash flows, the annual IRR equals 9.27\%.
A tax reserve is advertised at $5.9\%$ nominal, converted every six months. Its one-year accumulation corresponds to 5.85\%.
A conservation fund must grow by $35\%$ while earning continuously at $3.2\%$. It reaches that multiple after $9.38$ years.
A private note pays $1{,}200$ coupons in years 1 through 3 and returns $20{,}000$ with the final coupon in year 3. At $6.0\%$, the note's price is \$20{,}125.00.
A touring company contributes $8{,}000$ at year-end, reduces later contributions by $4\%$, and earns $5.5\%$ on the fund. After the fifth contribution, the balance is \$41{,}396.83.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

For one terminal inflow, the IRR is the compound rate that makes discounted inflow equal initial cost.

$$0=-42000.00+\frac{71500.00}{(1+r)^6}$$

$$42000.00(1+r)^6=71500.00$$

$$1+r=\left(\frac{71500.00}{42000.00}\right)^{1/6}$$

$$r=0.09272143$$

$$100r=9.2721\%$$

The computed internal rate of return is 9.27\%, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

An effective annual rate must reproduce the accumulation from every compounding period in the year.

$$i_p=\frac{0.0590}{2}=0.029500$$

$$1+R=(1+i_p)^{2}=(1+0.029500)^{2}$$

$$R=(1+0.029500)^{2}-1=0.05987025$$

$$100R=5.9870\%$$

The computed effective annual rate is 5.99\%, not 5.85\%, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

The time is unknown, so take natural logarithms in the continuous accumulation equation.

$$1.3500=e^{0.0320t}$$

$$\ln(1.3500)=0.0320t$$

$$t=\frac{\ln(1.3500)}{0.0320}$$

$$t=9.378269$$

The computed elapsed time is $9.38$ years, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

At the final deposit date, each growing contribution has earned a different number of interest periods.

$$FV=\sum_{k=0}^{4}8000.00(1+-0.0400)^k(1+0.0550)^{4-k}$$

$$FV=8000.00(1+0.0550)^{4}\sum_{k=0}^{4}\left(\frac{1+-0.0400}{1+0.0550}\right)^k$$

$$FV=8000.00(1+0.0550)^{4}\frac{1-0.90995261^5}{1-0.90995261}$$

$$FV=41396.826005$$

The computed accumulated balance is \$41{,}396.83, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 9
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: An endowment rose from $50{,}000$ to $63{,}500$ in six years under continuous compounding. Its force of interest was 3.98\%.
An acquisition earnout delivers $25{,}000$ after two years and $40{,}000$ after five years. With capital priced at $8.2\%$, the buyer books a liability of \$48{,}746.96.
A cooperative saves $2{,}500$ after its first harvest and lets deposits grow $8\%$ annually while the account yields $4.5\%$. Just after the seventh deposit, the cooperative has \$25{,}211.60.
A film cooperative invests $1{,}200$ at each quarter-end for 20 quarters. Its quarterly yield is $1.1\%$, giving \$26{,}876.55 at quarter 20.
A farm's $360{,}000$ mortgage uses 288 payments and a $0.46\%$ monthly rate. Immediately after installment 96, its balance is \$287{,}526.80.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Use both observed values to solve for the force of interest in the exponential model.

$$63500.00=50000.00e^{r(6)}$$

$$e^{6r}=\frac{63500.00}{50000.00}=1.27000000$$

$$6r=\ln(1.27000000)$$

$$r=\frac{\ln(1.27000000)}{6}=0.03983615$$

$$100r=3.9836\%$$

The computed continuous annual rate is 3.98\%, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Each dated cash flow requires its own discount exponent before the values can be added.

$$PV=\sum_{t}\frac{C_t}{(1+i)^t}$$

$$PV=\frac{25000.00}{(1+0.0820)^2}+\frac{40000.00}{(1+0.0820)^5}$$

$$PV_2=\frac{25000.00}{(1+0.0820)^2}=21354.307249$$

$$PV_5=\frac{40000.00}{(1+0.0820)^5}=26972.654379$$

$$PV=21354.307249+26972.654379$$

$$PV=48326.961628$$

The computed present value is \$48{,}326.96, not \$48{,}746.96, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

At the final deposit date, each growing contribution has earned a different number of interest periods.

$$FV=\sum_{k=0}^{6}2500.00(1+0.0800)^k(1+0.0450)^{6-k}$$

$$FV=2500.00(1+0.0450)^{6}\sum_{k=0}^{6}\left(\frac{1+0.0800}{1+0.0450}\right)^k$$

$$FV=2500.00(1+0.0450)^{6}\frac{1-1.03349282^7}{1-1.03349282}$$

$$FV=25211.602737$$

The computed accumulated balance is \$25{,}211.60, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

An ordinary annuity accumulates every end-of-period payment to the date of the last payment.

$$s_{\overline{20}|}=\frac{(1+0.01100)^20-1}{0.01100}$$

$$FV=1200.00s_{\overline{20}|}$$

$$FV=1200.00\frac{(1+0.01100)^20-1}{0.01100}$$

$$FV=26681.546485$$

The computed annuity future value is \$26{,}681.55, not \$26{,}876.55, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=360000.00\frac{0.004600}{1-(1+0.004600)^{-288}}$$

$$PMT=2258.176536$$

$$n_{\mathrm{remaining}}=288-96=192$$

$$B_96=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-192}}{i}$$

$$B_96=287526.799220$$

The computed balance after payment 96 is \$287{,}526.80, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 10
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Alumni pledge $10{,}000$ one year from now, $12{,}000$ three years from now, and $14{,}000$ four years from now. The scholarship office uses $5.0\%$ and recognizes \$31{,}202.70.
A warranty program expects $15{,}000$ of claims in its first year and $82\%$ of the previous year's claims in each of the next seven years. The eight-year forecast totals \$66{,}298.83.
A family office withdraws $10{,}000$ today and at every year-start forever. At $5\%$, the perpetuity-due needs \$207{,}000.00.
On a $150{,}000$ office loan with 120 payments at $0.58\%$ monthly, \$868.54 of payment 1 goes toward principal.
A mobile clinic outlay of \$320{,}000 leads to benefits of $100{,}000$ in years 2 and 3 and $180{,}000$ in year 6. At $6.8\%$, its NPV is -\$30{,}193.87.
tactical_explanations:
**B.** → True

A constant percentage change makes the scheduled amounts a finite geometric progression.

$$C_k=15000.00(0.82000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_8=\sum_{k=1}^{8}15000.00(0.82000)^{k-1}$$

$$S_8=15000.00\frac{0.82000^{8}-1}{0.82000-1}$$

$$S_8=66298.826178$$

The computed schedule total is \$66{,}298.83, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The infinite payment stream converges because its discount rate exceeds its growth rate.

$$PV_1=\sum_{t=1}^\infty\frac{10000.00(1+0.0000)^{t-1}}{(1+0.0500)^t}$$

$$PV_1=\frac{10000.00}{0.0500-0.0000}$$

$$PV_1=200000.000000$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=(1+0.0500)PV_1$$

$$PV_{\mathrm{due}}=210000.000000$$

The computed perpetuity present value is \$210{,}000.00, not \$207{,}000.00, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

The mortgage principal equals the present value of its level month-end payments.

$$P=PMT\frac{1-(1+i)^{-n}}{i}$$

$$PMT=150000.00\frac{0.005800}{1-(1+0.005800)^{-120}}$$

$$PMT=1738.536438$$

$$I_1=150000.00(0.005800)=870.000000$$

$$PR_1=PMT-I_1=1738.536438-870.000000$$

$$PR_1=868.536438$$

The computed first principal reduction is \$868.54, matching the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 11
tasks.context: A cooperative deposits \$50{,}000 in a one-year certificate quoting $7.2\%$ nominal interest compounded quarterly. No money enters or leaves during the year. The periodic rate is one fourth of the quote, and the certificate compounds through four complete quarters. The treasurer must reconcile the periodic rate, annual factor, effective yield, and maturity value.
statements: The quarterly rate is $1.8\%$.
The effective annual rate is $7.20\%$.
The annual accumulation factor is $1.073967$.
The maturity value is \$53{,}600.00.
Quarterly compounding adds less than $0.10$ percentage point.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared periodic calculation gives $1.8\%$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → False

The shared effective rate is $7.3967\%$, not $7.20\%$.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**C.** → True

The shared factor rounds to $1.073967$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**D.** → False

The shared maturity value is \$53{,}698.37.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → False

The shared lift is about $0.197$ percentage point.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.1.

Shared solution:
1. Use nominal rate $j=0.072$ and $m=4$ quarters.
2. The periodic rate is $i_q=j/m$.
3. Thus $i_q=0.072/4=0.018$.
4. The one-year factor is $(1+i_q)^4$.
5. Substitute $(1.018)^4$.
6. The factor is $1.07396743$.
7. The effective rate is factor minus one.
8. Thus $i_{eff}=0.07396743$.
9. As a percentage, this is $7.3967\%$.
10. The maturity value is $50000(1.07396743)$.
11. Thus the value is \$53{,}698.37.
12. The effective-rate lift is $7.3967-7.2000=0.1967$ points.
13. Use these shared values for every claim.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 12
tasks.context: A legal reserve starts with \$82{,}000 and earns a continuous annual force of interest of $4.3\%$ for six years. There are no deposits, withdrawals, fees, or taxes. The analyst uses the exponential model for the six-year balance and also records the dollar growth and the model's doubling time. Every claim refers to this same reserve.
statements: The six-year growth factor is $e^{0.258}$.
The six-year balance is \$106{,}135.78.
The reserve earns \$24{,}135.78 over six years.
Its continuous doubling time is $15.12$ years.
Using $(1.043)^6$ is the stated continuous model.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared exponent is exactly $0.258$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared balance rounds to \$106{,}135.78.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → True

Subtracting \$82{,}000 gives the stated growth.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**D.** → False

The shared doubling time is $16.12$ years.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → False

The shared model uses $e^{rt}$, not discrete annual powers.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.2.

Shared solution:
1. Use the continuous model $A=Pe^{rt}$.
2. Set $P=82000$, $r=0.043$, and $t=6$.
3. The exponent is $rt=0.043(6)$.
4. Thus $rt=0.258$.
5. The growth factor is $e^{0.258}$.
6. Numerically, the factor is $1.29433882$.
7. Multiply by the initial reserve.
8. This gives $A=82000(1.29433882)$.
9. The six-year balance is \$106{,}135.78.
10. Dollar growth is $A-P$.
11. Thus growth is \$24{,}135.78.
12. Doubling solves $2=e^{0.043t}$.
13. Hence $t=\ln 2/0.043=16.12$ years.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 13
tasks.context: A patent settlement pays \$12{,}000 after one year, \$18{,}000 after three years, and \$25{,}000 after five years. The owner values all three payments at time zero using a $6\%$ effective annual discount rate. There are no other cash flows. The valuation team discounts each payment by its own date before adding the present values.
statements: The first payment is worth \$11{,}320.75 today.
The third payment is discounted for two years.
The final payment is worth \$20{,}681.45 today.
The settlement's present value is \$45{,}115.36.
The undiscounted payments total \$45{,}115.36.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared one-year present value is \$11{,}320.75.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → False

The shared timeline places that payment at year 3.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**C.** → False

The shared final present value is \$18{,}681.45.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → True

The shared sum rounds to \$45{,}115.36.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**E.** → False

The nominal total is \$55{,}000.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.3.

Shared solution:
1. Use $PV=\sum C_t(1.06)^{-t}$.
2. Discount the first payment for one year.
3. $PV_1=12000/1.06=11320.75$.
4. Discount the second payment for three years.
5. $PV_3=18000/(1.06)^3=15113.15$.
6. Discount the final payment for five years.
7. $PV_5=25000/(1.06)^5=18681.45$.
8. Add the three present values.
9. $PV=11320.75+15113.15+18681.45$.
10. Thus $PV=45115.36$.
11. The undiscounted total is $12000+18000+25000$.
12. That nominal total is \$55{,}000.
13. Use the dated values rather than one common exponent.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 14
tasks.context: A research grant pays six annual installments. The first installment is \$6{,}000 at the end of year 1, and each later installment is exactly $5\%$ larger than the preceding one. The amounts are not discounted in this budget report. The administrator needs the common ratio, selected installments, and the full six-payment commitment from one geometric schedule.
statements: The installment ratio is $1.05$.
The third installment is \$6{,}615.00.
The sixth installment is \$7{,}657.69.
All six installments total \$39{,}811.48.
The schedule is an arithmetic sequence.
tactical_explanations:

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared third term is \$6{,}615.00.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → True

The shared sixth term rounds to \$7{,}657.69.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**D.** → False

The shared total is \$40{,}811.48.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → False

The shared ratio is constant, not the dollar difference.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.4.

Shared solution:
1. Use first term $a=6000$.
2. A $5\%$ increase gives ratio $q=1.05$.
3. The installment formula is $C_k=6000(1.05)^{k-1}$.
4. The second installment is \$6{,}300.00.
5. The third installment is \$6{,}615.00.
6. The fourth installment is \$6{,}945.75.
7. The fifth installment is \$7{,}293.04.
8. The sixth installment is \$7{,}657.69.
9. Use $S_6=a(q^6-1)/(q-1)$.
10. Substitute $6000((1.05)^6-1)/0.05$.
11. This gives $S_6=40811.476875$.
12. The total rounds to \$40{,}811.48.
13. A constant percentage change makes the schedule geometric.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 15
tasks.context: A company signs a three-year equipment lease requiring 36 payments of \$2{,}400 at each month-end. The monthly valuation rate is $0.5\%$, and no payment is due at signing. The accountant values the ordinary annuity at signing and also calculates what the same payment stream accumulates to immediately after payment 36. Timing and rate remain fixed throughout.
statements: The signing liability is \$78{,}890.44.
The month-36 accumulated value is \$94{,}406.65.
The first payment is discounted for zero months.
An annuity-due value would be \$79{,}000.00.
There are 35 month-end payments in the contract.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared ordinary-annuity present value gives this liability.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared accumulated value rounds to the stated amount.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → False

The first month-end payment is discounted one month.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → False

The shared one-period timing shift gives \$79{,}284.89.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → False

The shared contract specifies 36 payments.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.5.

Shared solution:
1. Use monthly rate $i=0.005$ and $n=36$.
2. The payments form an ordinary annuity.
3. Use $PV=2400[1-(1.005)^{-36}]/0.005$.
4. The annuity present-value factor is $32.871016$.
5. Direct evaluation gives $PV=78890.438974$.
6. Thus the signing liability is \$78{,}890.44.
7. Use $FV=2400[(1.005)^{36}-1]/0.005$.
8. Direct evaluation gives $FV=94406.651915$.
9. Thus the month-36 value is \$94{,}406.65.
10. The first month-end payment is discounted one month.
11. An annuity due shifts every payment one month earlier.
12. Its present value would be $PV(1.005)$.
13. That shifted value is \$79{,}284.89.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 16
tasks.context: A clinic borrows \$320{,}000 and repays it with 240 equal month-end payments at a monthly rate of $0.45\%$. The rate and payment stay fixed, and payments are made exactly as scheduled. The controller wants the payment, first-month split, balance just after payment 60, and total scheduled interest, all from this single amortization model.
statements: The monthly payment is \$2{,}183.21.
First-month interest is \$1{,}430.00.
Payment 1 reduces principal by \$743.21.
The balance after payment 60 is \$286{,}938.30.
Total scheduled interest is \$203{,}969.22.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared payment rounds to \$2{,}183.21.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → False

The shared opening interest calculation gives \$1{,}440.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**C.** → True

The shared payment less interest gives \$743.21.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**D.** → False

The shared remaining-payment value is \$268{,}938.30.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → True

The shared total-payment calculation gives this interest.

The shared result makes the claim True.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.6.

Shared solution:
1. Use principal $P=320000$, $i=0.0045$, and $n=240$.
2. Set $P=PMT[1-(1+i)^{-n}]/i$.
3. Solve $PMT=P i/[1-(1+i)^{-n}]$.
4. The payment is $2183.205089$.
5. Thus $PMT=\$2{,}183.21$.
6. First-month interest is $320000(0.0045)=1440$.
7. First principal reduction is $2183.205089-1440$.
8. Thus principal reduction is \$743.21.
9. After payment 60, 180 payments remain.
10. Value those payments at month 60.
11. The balance is \$268{,}938.30.
12. Total payments are $240(2183.205089)$.
13. Subtracting principal gives total interest \$203{,}969.22.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 17
tasks.context: A recycling project costs \$200{,}000 today and returns \$70{,}000 after year 1, \$85{,}000 after year 3, and \$100{,}000 after year 5. Management uses a $7\%$ effective annual hurdle rate and has no other project cash flows. The analyst discounts every return separately, computes NPV, and applies the rule that a positive NPV supports acceptance.
statements: The year-1 return is worth \$65{,}420.56 today.
The three returns have present value \$205{,}104.50.
The project's NPV is -\$6{,}104.50.
The NPV rule supports accepting the project.
The undiscounted net gain is \$65{,}000.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared year-1 discount gives this amount.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → False

The shared three-return sum is \$206{,}104.50, not \$205{,}104.50.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**C.** → False

The shared NPV is positive, not negative.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → True

The shared NPV is positive.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**E.** → False

The shared nominal net gain is \$55{,}000.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.7.

Shared solution:
1. Write the initial cost as a time-zero outflow of \$200{,}000.
2. Discount year 1 by $(1.07)^1$.
3. Its present value is \$65{,}420.56.
4. Discount year 3 by $(1.07)^3$.
5. Its present value is \$69{,}385.32.
6. Discount year 5 by $(1.07)^5$.
7. Its present value is \$71{,}298.62.
8. Add the three discounted returns.
9. Their present value is \$206{,}104.50.
10. Subtract the \$200{,}000 initial cost.
11. The NPV is positive \$6{,}104.50.
12. A positive NPV supports acceptance.
13. Undiscounted net gain is $255000-200000=\$55{,}000$.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 18
tasks.context: A savings account promises an $8.5\%$ effective annual yield but advertises a nominal annual rate compounded monthly. The monthly rate must reproduce the promised one-year accumulation over 12 equal periods. No deposits or withdrawals affect the comparison. Compliance calculates the monthly periodic rate, the nominal quote, and the one-year factor from one equivalence equation.
statements: The monthly rate is about $0.68215\%$.
The nominal monthly-convertible quote is $8.1858\%$.
The monthly rate is exactly $8.5\%/12$.
Twelve monthly periods reproduce a factor of $1.085$.
The nominal quote must exceed $8.5\%$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared root calculation gives $0.682149\%$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared nominal conversion gives $8.1858\%$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → False

The shared monthly rate comes from a twelfth root.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → True

The shared equivalence equation has factor $1.085$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**E.** → False

The shared nominal rate is lower than $8.5\%$.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.1.

Shared solution:
1. Set the effective one-year factor to $1.085$.
2. Let $i_m$ be the equivalent monthly rate.
3. Use $(1+i_m)^{12}=1.085$.
4. Take the positive twelfth root.
5. $i_m=(1.085)^{1/12}-1$.
6. This gives $i_m=0.006821493$.
7. As a percentage, $i_m=0.682149\%$.
8. Let $j^{(12)}=12i_m$.
9. Then $j^{(12)}=0.081857920$.
10. The nominal quote is $8.1858\%$.
11. Compounding its monthly rate gives $1.085$.
12. Simple division $0.085/12$ ignores monthly compounding.
13. The equivalent nominal quote is below the effective rate.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 19
tasks.context: A machine has a current book value of \$150{,}000 and depreciates continuously at an annual force of $6.2\%$ for five years. No upgrades or additional write-downs occur. The accounting model is $V(t)=V_0e^{-dt}$. The review computes the five-year value, total modeled loss, remaining proportion, and continuous half-life from this one setup.
statements: The five-year exponent is $-0.31$.
The five-year book value is \$110{,}017.04.
The modeled loss is \$40{,}982.96.
The remaining proportion is about $80.01\%$.
The continuous half-life is $10.18$ years.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared rate-time product is $-0.31$.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared exponential value gives this amount.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → False

The shared loss is \$39{,}982.96, not \$40{,}982.96.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → False

The shared remaining proportion is about $73.34\%$.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**E.** → False

The shared half-life is $11.18$ years.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.2.

Shared solution:
1. Use $V(t)=V_0e^{-dt}$.
2. Set $V_0=150000$, $d=0.062$, and $t=5$.
3. The exponent is $-0.062(5)=-0.31$.
4. The remaining factor is $e^{-0.31}$.
5. This factor is approximately $0.73344696$.
6. Multiply the factor by \$150{,}000.
7. The five-year value is \$110{,}017.04.
8. Subtract from the initial book value.
9. The modeled loss is \$39{,}982.96.
10. The remaining percentage is $73.3447\%$.
11. Half-life solves $0.5=e^{-0.062t}$.
12. Thus $t=\ln 2/0.062$.
13. The half-life is $11.18$ years.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 20
tasks.context: An estate pays an heir \$10{,}000 immediately, \$20{,}000 after two years, and \$30{,}000 after six years. The executor values the package at a $5.5\%$ effective annual rate. The immediate payment is already at time zero, while each later amount has its own discount exponent. There are no other estate payments in this calculation.
statements: The immediate payment has present value \$10{,}000.
The year-2 payment is worth \$17{,}969.05 today.
The year-6 payment is worth \$21{,}500.00 today.
The package is worth \$49{,}726.42 today.
Discounting all three for six years gives the same value.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The shared timeline places this payment at time zero.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**B.** → True

The shared two-year discount gives this amount.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**C.** → False

The shared six-year value is \$21{,}757.37, not \$21{,}500.00.

The shared result makes the claim False.

**D.** → True

The shared sum rounds to \$49{,}726.42.

The shared result makes the claim True.

**E.** → False

The shared timeline requires exponents zero, two, and six.

The shared result makes the claim False.
tasks.solution_overview:
Topics: 3.3.

Shared solution:
1. Use time zero as the valuation date.
2. The immediate \$10{,}000 needs no discounting.
3. Thus $PV_0=\$10{,}000.00$.
4. Discount \$20{,}000 for two years.
5. $PV_2=20000/(1.055)^2$.
6. This gives $PV_2=\$17{,}969.05$.
7. Discount \$30{,}000 for six years.
8. $PV_6=30000/(1.055)^6$.
9. This gives $PV_6=\$21{,}757.37$.
10. Add the three time-zero values.
11. $PV=10000+17969.05+21757.37$.
12. The total present value is \$49{,}726.42.
13. Different payment dates require different exponents.
